prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the geometry of an indoor cafe/store across five frames as the camera wearer turns from facing a drink refrigerator and pastry case on the left (frames 1–2) toward a checkout counter on the left, a bakery display case on the right, and a back counter with beverage dispensers 3.5–4.5 m away (frames 3–5). In frame 1, a person in a red and white hooded jacket stands very close on the right within arm's reach (~0.6–0.8 m), partially occluding the refrigerator ~2.5 m behind them, before moving leftward in frame 2 (~1.5 m away) and reappearing standing at the left checkout counter in frame 5 (~1.5–1.8 m away, facing left away from the wearer and within arm's reach of the counter and POS terminal). In frames 3–5, a seated person in a dark hoodie, cap, and glasses is brightest in the lower foreground (~0.8–1.2 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer and ~1.5 m to the right of the standing person in frame 5), facing toward the camera wearer with their head tilted downward while shifting from center to bottom-right as the camera pans left. The depth map clearly separates foreground people from background fixtures—even during heavy motion blur in frame 2 where RGB boundaries smear—and resolves the recessed back counter (~4 m) relative to the mid-ground checkout counter (~1.8–2.2 m) and right pastry case (~1.8–2.0 m). However, the map looks unreliable inside glass surfaces (flattened shelving inside the refrigerator and pastry display), along softened object boundaries during frame 2's blur, and in the upper-left wall/corner areas where dark depth values overstate distance.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates key foreground entities across the five-frame pan, starting in frame 1 with two glass doors of the drink cooler (~2.5 m away) labeled as separate 'refrigerator' instances on the left, partially occluded on the right by the 'person' in the red jacket (~0.6–0.8 m away). In frame 2, as the camera turns right with heavy motion blur, it detects two overlapping 'person' masks on the left (~1.5–2.0 m away, within arm's reach of each other): the person in the red jacket and a second person standing just behind and to their left who is difficult to distinguish in the blurred RGB alone. In frames 3–5, it tracks the seated 'person' in the lower foreground (~0.8–1.2 m in front of the wearer, shifting from center to far right and cropped at the lower torso) and reveals a purple 'chair' mask directly behind their left shoulder in frame 4 (within their contact reach) that is nearly invisible against their dark clothing in RGB. By frame 5, it simultaneously segments the standing 'person' on the left (~1.5–1.8 m away, facing left toward the counter and cropped at the head and knees) and the seated 'person' on the bottom right (~1.0 m away, facing toward the camera wearer). However, the segmentation map is unreliable for scene layout and static fixtures, completely omitting the counters, POS screen, and pastry display cases across all frames, misclassifying snack packets on the left counter as a 'book' in frame 3 and a coffee dispenser in the back as a 'bottle' in frame 5, and bleeding the pink person mask across the frame boundary between frames 1 and 2.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, failing to render any body or hand skeletons despite multiple people being visible within 0.6–2.0 m of the camera wearer. From the RGB context, the person in the red jacket passes from right to left across frames 1–2 (moving from ~0.7 m to ~1.5 m away with their back and left side toward the wearer) and stands facing left at the checkout counter in frame 5 (~1.5–1.8 m away, with hands raised near the counter within arm's reach of the terminal), while a second person is briefly visible behind them on the far left in frame 2. Meanwhile, a seated person in a cap and glasses occupies the lower foreground in frames 3–5 (~0.8–1.2 m away, within arm's reach of the camera wearer), oriented toward the wearer with their head angled downward and raising their right hand near their face in frame 5. Because the pose detector outputs no keypoints at all, it provides no spatial information beyond the RGB image and fails to capture gaze direction, torso orientation, or hand positions. This total failure highlights the unreliability of the pose estimator under severe egocentric crop (only heads and upper torsos visible in frames 1, 3, and 4, and a headless torso in frame 5), rear/side views, and heavy motion blur in frame 2.
